title: Subscription health forensics — QBR triage template and escalation map
body:
Purpose: quick, pragmatic QBR-first forensic triage for subscriptions flagged at risk. Use this as the working template for the 48-72 hour analysis, plus an exec escalation map and a short bank of save plays. Keep versions lean and attach raw metrics tables from the linked spreadsheet.

Audience: CSMs doing pre-QBR audits, CS leadership triage, AMs prepping renewal conversations, and revops for impact measurement.

How to use (workflow):
- 0–24h: intake (owner = CSM) — collect metrics, customer-provided reasons for risk, last escalations.
- 24–48h: forensic deep-dive (owner = CSM + Solutions Eng) — run checklist below, identify primary driver(s) and confidence level.
- 48–72h: mitigation plan + canary rollout (owner = CSM + TL) — pick 1–2 quick save plays, assign owners, set success criteria.
- If criteria unmet: escalate per map (owner = CS Ops / Head of CS).

Quick intake fields (paste into QBR notes):
- Customer name:
- ARR / ARR at risk:
- Renewal date:
- Contract term left (months):
- CSM:
- Primary contact / economic buyer:
- Risk trigger (choose top 2): usage drop / product fit / price / exec change / security / SSO / outages / integration failure / competitor / procurement delay / billing dispute / other
- Last NPS / CSAT (30/90/365):
- Top 3 open escalations/tickets (IDs):
- Recent product changes impacting them (date + PR/Release):
- Recent ROI evidence (case studies, logs, velocity improvements):

Forensic checklist (data + qualitative): mark H/M/L confidence per item
- Usage telemetry: MAU/DAU, prompt volume, token spend trend (90/30/7 day).
- Error rates and latency spikes: correlated with customer sessions.
- Model behavior / quality regressions: any eval failures, hallucination incidents.
- Billing / quota throttles: any metered limits or unexpected overages.
- Security/compliance blockers: contract clauses, audit requests pending.
- Org changes at customer: new CTO/PM/Procurement flags.
- Contractual/PS engagement health: outstanding deliverables, SOW drift.
- ROI signals: metrics that matter to them (e.g., time saved, retention uplift).
- Competitive moves: new vendor PoC, pilot results shared.
- Exec sentiment: verbatim notes from sponsor / champion.

Primary-driver framing (choose one):
- Operability: product reliability or latency is causing churn risk.
- Fit: core use-case no longer maps to ROI.
- Commercial: price or terms misalignment.
- Org: stakeholders changed or procurement blocked.
- Security/Compliance: policy prevents deployment.

Confidence guide: H= >70% causal evidence, M=30–70%, L=<30%

Rapid mitigation playbook (pick 1–2 based on driver):
- Operability plays:
  - Fast patch: engineering hotfix + dedicated SRE handoff; promise 72-hour RCA and mitigation timeline.
  - Scoped downgrade: move to stable model variant / reduced seq length to guarantee latency SLOs for 2 weeks.
  - White-glove routing: dedicated infra for customer during canary window (temp reserved pool).
- Fit plays:
  - Use-case deep-dive workshop (Solutions Eng + CSM) within 5 business days; prepare 3 small success experiments.
  - Re-scope ROI metrics and propose 90-day proof-of-value with explicit KPIs and acceptance criteria.
- Commercial plays:
  - Short-term concession + conditional extension (e.g., 2 months credit in exchange for 1-year renewed term).
  - Pilot pricing: discounted pilot for new feature set with conversion milestones.
- Org/security plays:
  - Meet-with-stakeholders: coordinate SRE/security-to-security call; prepare architecture and compliance pack.
  - Offer private deployment (VPC) evaluation checklist + timeline estimate.

Exec escalation map (when to escalate):
- Level 1 (CS Lead): // immediate if confidence H & renewal < 90 days OR if revenue at risk > $50k ARR.
- Level 2 (Head of CS + Partner Eng): // required if Level 1 mitigation needs infra/product changes or commercial concession > $25k ARR.
- Level 3 (CEO + CRO): // required if mitigation cost > 3 months ARR or strategic account flagged by GTM.

Escalation packet (what to send at each level):
- One-page summary: primary driver, confidence, recommended play(s), asks (budget/engineering priority), 3 KPI success criteria.
- Supporting tab: 30/90/365 usage charts, ticket timeline, verbatim exec notes, contract snapshot.
- Risks and rollback plan: what happens if mitigation fails.

Exec-ready one-pager template (copyable):
- Title: Account health: <Customer> — renewal <date>
- One-liner: Primary risk = <driver> (confidence <H/M/L>); immediate ask = <e.g., 72h hotfix + $X concession>.
- Impact: $ at risk, product lines affected, cross-sell/up-sell impact.
- Plan: short play + owner, medium play + owner, decision date.
- Metrics to watch: retention signal, usage rebound %, incident count.

Save-plays bank (fast options we can stand up in 72h):
- 72h: concierge support + SLA bump for one month; targeted log access for their SRE; model downgrade to stable JVM.
- 7-day: targeted PoV with tracked KPIs + pilot discount.
- 14-day: technical audit + remediation plan led by Solutions Eng.
- Commercial: month-of-support credit + conditional price cap for 6 months.

Tracking & handoff: always copy RevOps and Billing when concessions are proposed. Use the linked spreadsheet (SHEET) to log weekly progress and whether criteria are met.

Open questions / decision points (CSM to answer in 24h):
- Can customer share last 3 months of usage logs? (yes/no)
- Is procurement on a fixed cycle that blocks quick extension? (yes/no)
- Which internal exec will be copied to the escalation packet? (name/email)

Post-mitigation review (30-day):
- Outcome: saved / downgraded / churned.
- Metrics: change in usage, incident rate, CSAT/NPS delta.
- Learning: update model, common root causes, playbook amendments.

Notes to self / quick links:
- Reuse the "one-pager" heading for exec emails; keep to 200 words.
- Add recording of the 30-minute post-mortem to shared folder: /customer-success/wins-or-fails/<customer>-forensics.
- If security is blocker, attach KBA (security pack) and timeline for Private deployment evaluation.

Draft talking points for CSM opening QBR (30–60s):
- "We ran a pre-QBR for the last 48 hours focused on the reliability incidents you reported. We’ve identified X as the main cause and proposed a short mitigation that we can execute immediately. Our ask today is Y so we can validate impact within 2–4 weeks."

Revision history (quick):
- 2026-02-20 Aisha P. initial draft
- 2026-02-26 added mitigation bank (Marcus L.)

- 2026-03-10 tidy + linked sheet

TODOs (next 48h):

- Run stakeholder map and confirm exec email (owner: CSM).
- If commercial concession proposed, create draft amendment and loop RevOps (owner: CS Lead).

End of document.
